sources_considered.why: Reports METR's February 2026 time horizon for Claude Opus 4.6 and METR's caveats.
Primary METR page with methodology and caveats on messier tasks and scaffolds. Its numbers are only in a chart.
ARC-AGI-3 results and the report that a custom harness lifted Opus 4.6's score sharply on one environment.
The table gives a revised Opus 4.6 50% horizon of 11h59m and an 80% horizon of 1h10m, but table cells are not quotable sentences. Noted only in the limitations.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Claude 4.6 Opus On METR: The numbers', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: METR’s latest measurements put Claude Opus 4.6 at a 50%-time horizon of approximately 14.5 hours, meaning the model can successfully complete tasks that would take a seasoned human professional more than a full workday roughly half the time.

evidence_items.explanation: A model current at the post date completed self-contained software tasks that take experts more than a workday about half the time. This cuts against a flat claim that LLMs struggle with long-horizon work.

evidence_items.locator: paragraph beginning 'There is one real methodological debate here'

receipt.public_excerpt: ARC's report says a Duke-built custom harness pushed Claude Opus 4.6 from 0.25% to 97.1% on a single environment variant called TR87.

evidence_items.explanation: On a test of long-horizon planning in novel environments, Opus 4.6 scored 0.25% overall. A human-built harness lifted it dramatically on one environment. This shows heavy dependence on human scaffolding.

receipt.public_excerpt: Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6 managed 0.25%, while xAI’s Grok-4.20 scored exactly zero. Humans, meanwhile, solved 100% of environments.

evidence_items.explanation: ARC-AGI-3 explicitly tests long-horizon planning with sparse feedback. Frontier LLMs scored under 1%, which supports 'struggle with long-horizon reasoning' outside well-specified tasks.

evidence_items.locator: FAQ 'Does an 8-hour time horizon mean that AI can automate all jobs?'

receipt.public_excerpt: In our original time horizon paper, we found that AI agents did worse on messier tasks. In follow-up work, we found that AI agent performance drops substantially when scoring AI performance holistically rather than algorithmically.

evidence_items.explanation: METR's own caveat limits how far its long time horizons transfer to messy real work. This tempers e1 without reversing it.

unresolved_gaps: No public measure of whether LLMs 'lack persistent goals' was found.
METR revised Opus 4.6's 50% horizon to about 12 hours, and its 80% horizon is about 1 hour (Wikipedia table). These figures could not be quoted as sentences.
Whether a 50% success rate on 12-hour tasks counts as 'struggling' depends on the reader's threshold.
